job.organization: Santa Clarita Community College District (CA) / College of the Canyons (CA)

items.item_text: 01. Do you possess a Bachelor’s degree or higher from an accredited college or university? If yes, please provide a legible copy of your college/university transcript in your application packet, with the degree(s) clearly visible. Copies of diplomas are not acceptable in lieu of college transcripts. If no, you do not meet the minimum qualifications for this position.
02. Please describe your experience performing and conducting extensive statistical and technical research and evaluation to include any direct experience with labor market information.
03. Please provide examples of any experience you have with specialized databases and information systems to support research.
04. Please describe your experience writing and preparing comprehensive reports as well as making oral presentations on research findings related to labor market information.
05. Please describe your background in developing and deploying surveys to regional colleges, business and industry partners, and the community.
06. Please provide examples of any participation or collaboration with regional or state forums and organizations dealing with research in community colleges.
07. Why do you want to work in this management position at College of the Canyons? What unique skills and aptitudes would you contribute to the Workforce and Economic Advancement team?

Assists the Director, COE in the planning, design, implementation, and dissemination of research and evaluation studies related to labor market trends and educational outcomes to support workforce development and educational planning.

Conducts extensive statistical and technical research and evaluation studies, including literature reviews. Designs, maintains, manipulates, and queries specialized databases and information systems to support research activities.

Implements research studies, including coordinating the analysis and tabulation of results. Analyzes data using appropriate software applications, such as Microsoft Excel, R, Tableau, or similar tools for data analysis, management, and visualization.

Assists the Director, COE in responding to inquiries and provides detailed and technical information regarding research projects, including Labor Market Information (LMI) used to support program recommendations.

Identifies and extracts data from a variety of sources; inspects and codes data in preparation for analysis; creates project documentation and databases; and interprets research findings to support data-informed decision making.
Presents research findings, analyses, and interpretation clearly and effectively in narrative, graphic, tabular, written, and oral formats.
Prepares, and maintains comprehensive reports and delivers presentations explaining labor market research findings, implications, and applicability to workforce and educational planning.
Designs, prepares and administers surveys to regional colleges, business and industry partners, and community stakeholders in support of research projects.
Assists the Director, COE in preparing quarterly and annual narrative reports, renewal documents, and other required documentation in accordance with applicable grant and contract requirements.
Assists the Director, COE in presenting research findings at local advisory board meetings, regional consortium meetings, community college planning events, conferences and employer-education forums.
Maintains datasets, research information systems, and organized archives of information and reports to support efficient data collection, analyses, reporting, and responses to research inquiries.

Consults with internal and external stakeholders regarding the analysis, compilation, and interpretation of data. Provides technical guidance regarding research design, survey development, and test validation. Responds to questions and requests for information regarding research-related activities.

Represents the Center of Excellence, as assigned by the Director, at regional and statewide forums and organizations addressing community college research, labor market information, and workforce development.
Performs other related duties as assigned.
Qualitative and quantitative research design, and data analyses techniques.
Gather, validate, and interpret data from a wide variety of sources, including literature and Internet searches.
Research and evaluation theory, design, methodology, sampling and analytical techniques.
Manage multiple assignments and projects by establish priorities for, planning, and organizing a variety of tasks. Utilize and maintain project details in project management system.
Technical research report writing.
Work accurately and independently while meeting schedules and timelines.
Research software applications for data analyses, data management, spreadsheet, presentation, graphics, and word processing software applications (such as R, and Microsoft Office Suite).
Exhibit a strong understanding of ethical, compliance, privacy and security issues; apply relevant policies and procedures related to access, security, and delivery of data and research.
Survey Administration software (e.g. Qualtrics, Survey Monkey).
Take responsibility and use professional judgment based on established guidelines and procedures.
Survey sampling, design, and research.
Type with speed and accuracy; make arithmetical calculations in like manner.
Collection and coding of data.
Provide appropriate information to the students, faculty, staff, and the public in a professional manner.
Understand and carry out oral and written directions.

Establish and maintain strong professional working relationships with campus academic and administrative offices, departments and programs, to ensure the quality and accuracy of data provided by those offices.
Committed to Student Access, Engagement, and Success.
Willing to take strategic risks related to student-oriented change.
Capable of building strong teams.
Motivated to establish urgency for improvement.
Able to plan lasting internal change.
Results-oriented, ensuring effective implementation, routine assessment of programs and continuous data-informed improvement.
Effective at communicating and listening to foster strong relationships, shared priorities, and inspire trust and action.
Considerate of fiscal responsibilities and sound operations.
Dedicated to entrepreneurial fundraising that aligns to student access, engagement, and success goals.
Effective in developing effective external partnerships to achieve broader aims for student success.
A supporter of consistent and on-going professional development initiatives, in pursuit of the college’s strategic goals.
Work effectively and demonstrate currency of knowledge with various forms of technology (hardware/software) utilized in providing high-quality services.
Communicate clearly and effectively orally and in writing.

Demonstrate clear evidence of sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, disability, and ethnic backgrounds of community college students, staff and the community.
A creative, innovative, energetic instructional leader; a technologically sophisticated professional who is skilled in various technology applications.
A fair-minded, ethical, and honest leader with excellent interpersonal and communication skills and the courage and integrity to lead and accept responsibility.
